votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) Looked for a downstream re-check in the Celery task, the facade, and the Temporal activities — none exists; the resolver at tasks.py:25 is only used by `_inbox_rereview_carve_out`. (2) Precedent: the ReviewHog counterpart `_start_review` (receivers.py:239-273) has the identical shape — one toggle check in the receiver, then a Temporal workflow start with no re-check — so the design treats the receiver's check as the gate for the initial review, and AGENTS.md:104-105 only promises that a toggle off mid-PR "stops new runs". The initial run was requested while the toggle was on. (3) Reachability/frequency: the window is Celery pickup latency plus retry backoff; a user would have to flip the setting in that window immediately after a signals TaskRun output save. The consequence is one review/approval on a bot draft PR the user had opted into seconds earlier, and later head-changing events still go through the toggle-checked carve-out and `dismiss_stale_approvals`. The refutation does not fully succeed (the gap is real and the fix is ~5 lines using the already-imported resolver), but the finding's `should_fix` overstates a near-zero-frequency race with a benign outcome; it is at most a `consider`.

votes.evidence:
Premise holds in the worktree. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1246) takes `acting_user_id` as a plain argument, stamps it into `inbox_review` at 1176-1181, and creates + starts the ReviewRun at 1226-1234 without ever loading `ReviewUserSettings` or calling the registered resolver. The only toggle check on this leg is upstream in the receiver (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:131-137 `if pr_url is not None and settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs:`), which runs before the `transaction.on_commit` -> `queue_inbox_pr_review` -> `.delay()` handoff (receivers.py:138-146, facade/api.py:147-155). Downstream, stamphog's Temporal activities only read `inbox_review` for attribution and gate bypass (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:175, 237, 451), never for the toggle. So nothing re-checks the toggle between the receiver and the sandbox run.

Reachability in production: the toggle is a real prod setting (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:294, exposed at api/settings.py:27), stamphog is in INSTALLED_APPS (posthog/settings/web.py:45), and the task is a `@shared_task(ignore_result=True, max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=5)` (tasks.py:1109) on the default Celery queue. The race window is: broker publish -> worker pickup (normally seconds) plus at most 3 retries at 5s, or >=60s per retry on GitHub rate limit (tasks.py:1163). So a user who flips the toggle off in the seconds-to-minutes after their implementation run saves its PR URL still gets one hosted Stamphog review. Reachable, but a narrow window and a one-run consequence.

Precedent that the codebase treats this as a real gate: the sibling ReviewHog leg deliberately re-checks `review_inbox_prs` inside its Temporal workflow at resolve time ("Inbox re-checks the receiver-side gate here for snapshot-at-resolve consistency", products/review_hog/backend/temporal/workflow.py:424-436), and the stamphog webhook leg re-checks via `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` on later pushes (tasks.py:202-217, receivers.py:143-158). The initial stamphog leg is the one path without an execution-time re-check.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) Looked for a toggle re-check inside the Celery task, the facade, or stamphog's Temporal activities/workflow - none exists; `inbox_review` is only used for attribution and to bypass bot/draft gates. (2) Checked whether the Celery handoff is effectively synchronous - it is not; `.delay()` runs after commit on a worker, with retry backoff that can stretch the window to minutes on GitHub failures. (3) Checked whether the more common case (user opts out before the TaskRun output save) is covered - it is, by the receiver check, which is why the blast radius is only the post-save window. (4) The receiver fires "on every TaskRun output save carrying the PR URL" (tasks.py:1124-1125), and the dedupe is head-keyed, so a refire does not create a second run; the defect is limited to one review per opted-out user per PR head. The refutation fails on correctness (the gate really is skipped) but succeeds on scale: the trigger requires a toggle flip inside a seconds-to-minutes window, and the cost is one unwanted hosted review, so this is a minor consistency gap rather than a should_fix. Cheap fix if taken: call `get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver()` at the top of `process_inbox_pr_review`, the same hook the webhook leg already uses.
